rules.condition: i_apb_psel is high, i_apb_penable is low (Setup phase) and the mst FSM is in IDLE
rules.statement: The mst block loads reg_req_payload with PWRITE, PADDR, PPROT, PSTRB, PWDATA (and PAUSER, PWUSER in APB5) and launches the request.

rules.quote: In the cycle where i_apb_psel is high and i_apb_penable is low (the Setup phase, REF-001 4.1) and the mst FSM is in IDLE, the mst block loads reg_req_payload with PWRITE, PADDR, PPROT, PSTRB, PWDATA and, in APB5, PAUSER, PWUSER, and launches the request: with the two-phase handshake reg_req toggles, with the four-phase handshake it rises.
rules.statement: With the two-phase handshake reg_req toggles; with the four-phase handshake reg_req rises.

rules.quote: All of this happens at one clock edge (DEC-016).
rules.statement: Loading reg_req_payload and launching the request happen at the same clock edge.

rules.quote: Request crossing. reg_req crosses through u_sync_req (N stages). The slv FSM sees the event, loads reg_apb_payload from reg_req_payload (the bundle has been stable for at least N destination periods), raises PSEL (Setup), and one cycle later PENABLE (Access).
rules.condition: slv FSM sees the request event after u_sync_req
rules.statement: The slv FSM loads reg_apb_payload from reg_req_payload, which has been stable for at least N destination periods, then raises PSEL (Setup).

rules.quote: The slv FSM sees the event, loads reg_apb_payload from reg_req_payload (the bundle has been stable for at least N destination periods), raises PSEL (Setup), and one cycle later PENABLE (Access).
rules.condition: after PSEL is raised for Setup
rules.statement: PENABLE (Access) is raised one cycle after PSEL.

rules.quote: The slv FSM waits in ACCESS until the completer drives PREADY.
rules.statement: The slv FSM waits in ACCESS until the completer drives PREADY.

rules.quote: At that edge it loads reg_resp_hold with PRDATA, PSLVERR, PRUSER, PBUSER, drops PSEL and PENABLE, and launches the acknowledge (toggle, or rise).
rules.statement: At that edge the slv block loads reg_resp_hold with PRDATA, PSLVERR, PRUSER, PBUSER, drops PSEL and PENABLE, and launches the acknowledge (toggle or rise).

rules.quote: The acknowledge crosses through u_sync_ack. With the two-phase handshake the mst FSM sees the event, loads the response output registers from reg_resp_hold, and raises PREADY for one cycle (state RESP).
rules.condition: two-phase handshake and mst FSM sees the acknowledge event via u_sync_ack
rules.statement: The mst FSM loads the response output registers from reg_resp_hold and raises PREADY for one cycle (state RESP).

rules.quote: With the four-phase handshake the mst FSM first drops the request, waits for the acknowledge to fall (the slv FSM waits in REQ0 for the request to fall and then drops the acknowledge), and then loads the response and raises PREADY.
rules.statement: The mst FSM first drops the request, waits for the acknowledge to fall, then loads the response and raises PREADY.

rules.quote: With the four-phase handshake the mst FSM first drops the request, waits for the acknowledge to fall (the slv FSM waits in REQ0 for the request to fall and then drops the acknowledge), and then loads the response and raises PREADY.
rules.condition: four-phase handshake, slv FSM in REQ0
rules.statement: The slv FSM waits in REQ0 for the request to fall and then drops the acknowledge.

rules.quote: The requester drives the next Setup phase in the cycle after the PREADY cycle; the mst FSM is back in IDLE and captures it.
rules.statement: The mst FSM returns to IDLE and captures the next Setup phase driven in the cycle after the PREADY cycle.

rules.quote: Wake-up (APB5). i_apb_pwakeup is registered in the mst block, crosses through u_sync_wk, and drives o_apb_pwakeup through a flip-flop in the slv block, together with an in-progress term.
rules.statement: i_apb_pwakeup is registered in the mst block, crosses through u_sync_wk, and drives o_apb_pwakeup through a flip-flop in the slv block together with an in-progress term.

rules.quote: At most one transfer is in flight; the FSMs are in IDLE only between transfers.
rules.statement: At most one transfer is in flight, and the FSMs are in IDLE only between transfers.

rules.quote: The request bundle and the response bundle change only while the handshake is not in the phase in which the other domain may load them (REQ-HS-002).
rules.statement: The request and response bundles change only while the handshake is not in the phase in which the other domain may load them.

rules.quote: The two-phase request and acknowledge bits are equal when no transfer is in flight; the four-phase bits are both 0.
rules.statement: With the two-phase handshake the request and acknowledge bits are equal; with the four-phase handshake both are 0.

rules.quote: PREADY of the requester side is high only in state RESP, one cycle per transfer.
rules.statement: Requester-side PREADY is high only in state RESP, for one cycle per transfer.

rules.quote: A completer-side PSEL is high only in states SETUP and ACCESS.
rules.statement: Completer-side PSEL is high only in states SETUP and ACCESS.

rules.statement: Every flip-flop that drives an APB output is reset to 0.

rules.quote: A transfer starts with the Setup phase (PSEL high, PENABLE low, one cycle), then the Access phase (PENABLE high), which ends in the cycle where PREADY is high.
rules.statement: A transfer starts with a one-cycle Setup phase (PSEL high, PENABLE low), followed by the Access phase (PENABLE high), which ends in the cycle where PREADY is high.

rules.quote: After PREADY the bus returns to IDLE or goes directly to the Setup phase of the next transfer.
rules.condition: after the cycle where PREADY is high
rules.statement: After PREADY the bus may return to IDLE or go directly to the Setup phase of the next transfer.

rules.quote: PADDR, PPROT, PENABLE, PWRITE, PAUSER, PSTRB and the active lanes of PWDATA (and PWUSER of a write) are valid whenever PSEL is high, so the bridge captures them in the Setup cycle.
rules.statement: PADDR, PPROT, PENABLE, PWRITE, PAUSER, PSTRB, active PWDATA lanes and PWUSER of a write are valid whenever PSEL is high; the bridge captures them in the Setup cycle.

rules.quote: PREADY is valid when PSEL and PENABLE are high.
rules.statement: PREADY is valid when PSEL and PENABLE are high.

rules.quote: PRDATA of a read, PSLVERR, PRUSER of a read and PBUSER are valid when PSEL, PENABLE and PREADY are high.
rules.condition: PSEL, PENABLE and PREADY are high
rules.statement: PRDATA of a read, PSLVERR, PRUSER of a read and PBUSER are valid when PSEL, PENABLE and PREADY are high.

rules.quote: PADDR, PPROT, PWRITE, PWDATA, PSTRB, PAUSER, PWUSER do not change between the Setup and the Access phase and while PREADY is low.
rules.condition: between the Setup and Access phase and while PREADY is low
rules.statement: PADDR, PPROT, PWRITE, PWDATA, PSTRB, PAUSER and PWUSER must not change between Setup and Access phase and while PREADY is low.

rules.quote: The bridge relies on this only for the Setup cycle of the requester side; it guarantees it on the completer side by loading the fields into reg_apb_payload once.
rules.statement: The bridge guarantees stability of the completer-side fields by loading them into reg_apb_payload once, relying on requester stability only in the Setup cycle.

rules.quote: The completer extends the Access phase by driving PREADY low; the bridge propagates this by raising the requester-side PREADY only after the completer-side PREADY.
rules.condition: completer extends the Access phase with PREADY low
rules.statement: The bridge raises the requester-side PREADY only after the completer-side PREADY.

rules.quote: PSLVERR is valid only in the last cycle of a transfer.
rules.statement: PSLVERR is valid only in the last cycle of a transfer.

rules.quote: A transfer with an error may or may not have changed the completer; a read with an error can return invalid data and the requester may still use it, so the bridge forwards PRDATA and PSLVERR together without masking.
rules.condition: a transfer completes with an error
rules.statement: The bridge forwards PRDATA and PSLVERR together without masking, even for a read with an error.

rules.quote: PSTRB must be low in a read.
rules.statement: PSTRB must be low in a read.

rules.quote: The bridge forwards PSTRB as received (DEC-028).
rules.statement: The bridge forwards PSTRB as received.

rules.statement: PWAKEUP must be glitch-free to be sampled asynchronously and must stay high until PREADY when high in the same cycle as PSEL.

rules.quote: PWAKEUP is synchronous to its clock and shall be glitch-free to be sampled asynchronously; it may be asserted before, during or after PSEL, shall stay high until PREADY when high in the same cycle as PSEL, and should be asserted one cycle before PSEL.
rules.statement: PWAKEUP may be asserted before, during or after PSEL.

rules.quote: PWAKEUP is synchronous to its clock and shall be glitch-free to be sampled asynchronously; it may be asserted before, during or after PSEL, shall stay high until PREADY when high in the same cycle as PSEL, and should be asserted one cycle before PSEL.
rules.statement: PWAKEUP should be asserted one cycle before PSEL.

rules.statement: PAUSER and PWUSER are valid with PSEL (PWUSER also with PWRITE) and keep their value through Setup and Access phases.

rules.quote: PAUSER and PWUSER are valid with PSEL (PWUSER also with PWRITE) and keep their value through the Setup and Access phases; PRUSER and PBUSER are valid in the PREADY cycle.
rules.statement: PRUSER and PBUSER are valid in the PREADY cycle.

rules.quote: Case: PENABLE high without a preceding Setup cycle; Legal behavior: None; Illegal / unsupported case: Requester breaks Figure 4-1; IP response: Ignored; no transfer starts (DEC-027); Requirement IDs: REQ-FUNC-001
rules.condition: PENABLE high without a preceding Setup cycle
rules.statement: The bridge ignores PENABLE high without a preceding Setup cycle and starts no transfer.

rules.quote: Case: Requester changes a field during the Access phase; Legal behavior: None; Illegal / unsupported case: Requester breaks REF-001 3.1; IP response: Not detected; the bridge uses the Setup values; Requirement IDs: REQ-FUNC-001
rules.condition: requester changes a field during the Access phase
rules.statement: The bridge does not detect the change and uses the values captured in the Setup phase.

rules.quote: Case: Completer never drives PREADY; Legal behavior: None (a completer must eventually answer); Illegal / unsupported case: Completer hangs; IP response: Bridge waits without limit (DEC-006); Requirement IDs: REQ-FUNC-005
rules.statement: The bridge waits without limit for the completer PREADY.

rules.quote: Case: One reset asserted alone, or a reset in the middle of a transfer; Legal behavior: Both resets asserted together; Illegal / unsupported case: Single reset; IP response: The transfer in flight is lost; single reset is not supported; Requirement IDs: REQ-RESET-002
rules.statement: A single reset asserted alone is not supported; both resets must be asserted together, and a transfer in flight is lost on reset.

rules.quote: Case: One reset asserted alone, or a reset in the middle of a transfer; Legal behavior: Both resets asserted together; Illegal / unsupported case: Single reset; IP response: The transfer in flight is lost; single reset is not supported; Requirement IDs: REQ-RESET-002
rules.condition: reset in the middle of a transfer
rules.statement: The transfer in flight is lost when reset is asserted mid-transfer.

rules.quote: Signal/event: Not applicable; Polarity: Not applicable; Assert condition: Not required (confirmed by user, 2026-10-25): the IP has no interrupt or event output; errors travel as PSLVERR of the transfer; Clear/deassert condition: Not applicable; Mask/priority: Not applicable; Crossing: Not applicable; Reset state: Not applicable
rules.statement: The IP has no interrupt or event output; errors travel as PSLVERR of the transfer.

rules.quote: Five crossings exist; no other path joins the two domains (REQ-CLK-002).
rules.statement: Only the five listed crossings (CDC-001 to CDC-005) join the CLK-MST and CLK-SLV domains; no other path exists between them.

rules.quote: The structure is a handshake with bundled data: the control bits are synchronized (CLK-01), and each bundle is held stable and loaded by the destination only after the control bit arrived, so no bundle bit passes through a synchronizer.
rules.condition: Crossing of data bundles between domains
rules.statement: Each data bundle must be held stable and loaded by the destination only after its control bit arrives, so no bundle bit passes through a synchronizer.

rules.quote: Crossing ID: CDC-001; From to: mst to slv; Signals: Request bundle reg_req_payload (LPARA_REQ_W bits: PWRITE, PADDR, PPROT, PSTRB, PWDATA, PAUSER, PWUSER); Structure: Hold register in mst, loaded at the launch edge of the request bit; loaded into reg_apb_payload in slv at the edge that sees the request event; no synchronizer; Reset handling: Both registers reset to 0; Constraints / verification: set_max_delay with the guard band, EXC-001; stability by SVA-011; TEST-002
rules.statement: The request bundle reg_req_payload must be held in mst, loaded at the launch edge of the request bit, and loaded into reg_apb_payload in slv at the edge that sees the request event, without a synchronizer.

rules.quote: Crossing ID: CDC-001; From to: mst to slv; Signals: Request bundle reg_req_payload (LPARA_REQ_W bits: PWRITE, PADDR, PPROT, PSTRB, PWDATA, PAUSER, PWUSER); Structure: Hold register in mst, loaded at the launch edge of the request bit; loaded into reg_apb_payload in slv at the edge that sees the request event; no synchronizer; Reset handling: Both registers reset to 0; Constraints / verification: set_max_delay with the guard band, EXC-001; stability by SVA-011; TEST-002
rules.statement: The request hold register reg_req_payload and reg_apb_payload must reset to 0.

rules.quote: Crossing ID: CDC-002; From to: mst to slv; Signals: Request bit reg_req (toggle or level); Structure: N-stage synchronizer u_sync_req (cell option PARA_APBCDC_CELL_TYPE), no logic between the flop and the first stage; Reset handling: Synchronizer stages reset to 0 by i_rst_n_slv; Constraints / verification: set_max_delay, EXC-002; TEST-015
rules.statement: reg_req must cross to slv through N-stage synchronizer u_sync_req with no logic between the flop and the first stage, its stages reset to 0 by i_rst_n_slv.

rules.quote: Crossing ID: CDC-003; From to: slv to mst; Signals: Acknowledge bit reg_ack (toggle or level); Structure: N-stage synchronizer u_sync_ack, no logic before the first stage; Reset handling: Reset to 0 by i_rst_n_mst; Constraints / verification: set_max_delay, EXC-003; TEST-015
rules.statement: reg_ack must cross to mst through N-stage synchronizer u_sync_ack with no logic before the first stage, reset to 0 by i_rst_n_mst.

rules.quote: Crossing ID: CDC-004; From to: slv to mst; Signals: Response bundle reg_resp_hold (LPARA_RESP_W bits: PRDATA, PSLVERR, PRUSER, PBUSER); Structure: Hold register in slv, loaded at the launch edge of the acknowledge bit; loaded into reg_resp_payload in mst at the edge that sees the acknowledge event; no synchronizer; Reset handling: Both registers reset to 0; Constraints / verification: set_max_delay with the guard band, EXC-004; TEST-003
rules.statement: reg_resp_hold must be held in slv, loaded at the launch edge of the acknowledge bit, and loaded into reg_resp_payload in mst at the edge that sees the acknowledge event, without a synchronizer.

rules.quote: Crossing ID: CDC-004; From to: slv to mst; Signals: Response bundle reg_resp_hold (LPARA_RESP_W bits: PRDATA, PSLVERR, PRUSER, PBUSER); Structure: Hold register in slv, loaded at the launch edge of the acknowledge bit; loaded into reg_resp_payload in mst at the edge that sees the acknowledge event; no synchronizer; Reset handling: Both registers reset to 0; Constraints / verification: set_max_delay with the guard band, EXC-004; TEST-003
rules.statement: reg_resp_hold and reg_resp_payload must reset to 0.

rules.quote: Crossing ID: CDC-005; From to: mst to slv; Signals: Wake-up reg_wakeup (registered copy of i_apb_pwakeup, APB5 only); Structure: N-stage synchronizer u_sync_wk; Reset handling: Reset to 0 by i_rst_n_slv; Constraints / verification: set_max_delay, EXC-005; TEST-009
rules.statement: reg_wakeup, a registered copy of i_apb_pwakeup, must cross to slv through N-stage synchronizer u_sync_wk, reset to 0 by i_rst_n_slv.

rules.quote: Reset-domain crossing: the two resets are asserted together and released synchronously to their own clock, outside the IP (DEC-009). The two resets are asserted together.
rules.statement: The two resets are asserted together and each released synchronously to its own clock, outside the IP.

rules.quote: A release in one domain while the other is still in reset is allowed: the other domain's flip-flops are at their reset values, so a request cannot be launched or seen (the mst FSM leaves IDLE only on a Setup phase, which the requester does not start before its reset is released).
rules.condition: One domain released while the other is still in reset
rules.statement: Release of one reset while the other domain is still in reset is allowed; no request is launched or seen because the mst FSM leaves IDLE only on a Setup phase.

rules.quote: Reset ID: RST-MST; Port: i_rst_n_mst; Polarity / assertion: Active-low; Sync or async: Asynchronous assertion; release synchronous to i_clk_mst, made outside the IP; Scope: All state of the mst block and its synchronizer: hold register, request bit, wake-up register, response output registers, FSM; Deassertion: Synchronous to i_clk_mst; Reset value: All registers 0, FSM IDLE, o_apb_pready and o_apb_pslverr 0
rules.statement: On i_rst_n_mst assertion (active-low, asynchronous), all mst-block state resets: registers 0, FSM IDLE, o_apb_pready and o_apb_pslverr 0.

rules.quote: Reset ID: RST-SLV; Port: i_rst_n_slv; Polarity / assertion: Active-low; Sync or async: Asynchronous assertion; release synchronous to i_clk_slv, made outside the IP; Scope: All state of the slv block and its synchronizers: payload register, response hold register, acknowledge bit, FSM, o_apb_psel, o_apb_penable, o_apb_pwakeup; Deassertion: Synchronous to i_clk_slv; Reset value: All registers 0, FSM IDLE
rules.statement: On i_rst_n_slv assertion (active-low, asynchronous), all slv-block state resets: registers 0, FSM IDLE, including o_apb_psel, o_apb_penable and o_apb_pwakeup.

rules.quote: The IP contains no reset synchronizer: the two resets reach the IP already synchronized (rule RST-02 is met outside the IP, DEC-009).
rules.statement: The IP must contain no reset synchronizer; both resets must arrive already synchronized.

rules.quote: No transfer starts before both are released; the requester model of the verification keeps i_apb_psel low until then.
rules.statement: No transfer may start before both resets are released; the requester keeps i_apb_psel low until then.

rules.quote: The stopped-clock, warm-reset and retention cases are not supported.
rules.statement: Stopped-clock, warm-reset and retention cases are not supported.

rules.quote: Not required (confirmed by user, 2026-10-25): the IP is in one always-on power domain of the SoC and has no isolation, retention or power sequencing of its own.
rules.statement: The IP has no isolation, retention or power sequencing of its own; it sits in one always-on power domain.

rules.quote: The IP has no elaboration check for illegal values (REQ-PARAM-001).
rules.statement: The IP does not include an elaboration check for illegal parameter values (REQ-PARAM-001).

rules.quote: Parameter: PARA_APBCDC_ADDR_W; Purpose: Width of the byte address; Default: 32; Legal values / range: 1 to 32; Dependencies / invalid combinations: None; Effect: Width of PADDR and of the request bundle
rules.statement: PARA_APBCDC_ADDR_W, default 32 and legal range 1 to 32, sets the width of PADDR and of the request bundle.

rules.quote: Parameter: PARA_APBCDC_DATA_W; Purpose: Width of the data buses; Default: 32; Legal values / range: 8, 16 or 32; Dependencies / invalid combinations: None; Effect: Width of PWDATA, PRDATA; PSTRB has DATA_W / 8 bits
rules.statement: PARA_APBCDC_DATA_W, default 32 and legal values 8, 16 or 32, sets the width of PWDATA and PRDATA; PSTRB has DATA_W/8 bits.

rules.quote: Parameter: PARA_APBCDC_APB5; Purpose: Interface revision: 0 = APB4, 1 = APB5; Default: 0; Legal values / range: 0 or 1; Dependencies / invalid combinations: The user widths apply only when 1; Effect: APB5 adds PWAKEUP and the user signals
rules.statement: PARA_APBCDC_APB5 selects APB4 (0, default) or APB5 (1); APB5 adds PWAKEUP and the user signals, and user widths apply only when 1.

rules.quote: Parameter: PARA_APBCDC_USER_REQ_W; Purpose: Width of PAUSER; Default: 0; Legal values / range: 0 to 128; Dependencies / invalid combinations: Only with PARA_APBCDC_APB5 = 1; Effect: 0 = no PAUSER
rules.statement: PARA_APBCDC_USER_REQ_W (0 to 128, default 0) sets the width of PAUSER, only with PARA_APBCDC_APB5 = 1; 0 means no PAUSER.

rules.quote: Parameter: PARA_APBCDC_USER_DATA_W; Purpose: Width of PWUSER and PRUSER; Default: 0; Legal values / range: 0 to PARA_APBCDC_DATA_W; an integer multiple of 8 is recommended (REF-001 3.7.3); Dependencies / invalid combinations: Only with PARA_APBCDC_APB5 = 1; Effect: 0 = no PWUSER, no PRUSER
rules.statement: PARA_APBCDC_USER_DATA_W (0 to DATA_W, default 0) sets the width of PWUSER and PRUSER, only with APB5 = 1; 0 means none.

rules.quote: Parameter: PARA_APBCDC_USER_DATA_W; Purpose: Width of PWUSER and PRUSER; Default: 0; Legal values / range: 0 to PARA_APBCDC_DATA_W; an integer multiple of 8 is recommended (REF-001 3.7.3); Dependencies / invalid combinations: Only with PARA_APBCDC_APB5 = 1; Effect: 0 = no PWUSER, no PRUSER
rules.statement: PARA_APBCDC_USER_DATA_W should be an integer multiple of 8 (REF-001 3.7.3).

rules.quote: Parameter: PARA_APBCDC_USER_RESP_W; Purpose: Width of PBUSER; Default: 0; Legal values / range: 0 to 16; Dependencies / invalid combinations: Only with PARA_APBCDC_APB5 = 1; Effect: 0 = no PBUSER
rules.statement: PARA_APBCDC_USER_RESP_W (0 to 16, default 0) sets the width of PBUSER, only with PARA_APBCDC_APB5 = 1; 0 means no PBUSER.

rules.quote: Parameter: PARA_APBCDC_HS_TYPE; Purpose: Handshake: 0 = two-phase (toggle), 1 = four-phase (level); Default: 0; Legal values / range: 0 or 1; Dependencies / invalid combinations: None; Effect: Latency and number of crossing events; the function on the APB interfaces is the same
rules.statement: PARA_APBCDC_HS_TYPE selects two-phase toggle (0, default) or four-phase level (1) handshake; latency and crossing events differ but APB interface function is the same.

rules.quote: Parameter: PARA_APBCDC_CELL_TYPE; Purpose: Synchronizer cell option: 0 = bypass (simulation only), 1 = two D flip-flop cells, 2 = one 2-FF cell, 3 = one 3-FF cell, 4 = one 4-FF cell; Default: 2; Legal values / range: 0 to 4; Dependencies / invalid combinations: 0 is rejected by the SDC; Effect: Number of stages N = 2, 2, 3, 4 for the values 1 to 4
rules.statement: PARA_APBCDC_CELL_TYPE (0 to 4, default 2) selects the synchronizer cell option, with N = 2, 2, 3, 4 stages for values 1 to 4.

rules.quote: Parameter: PARA_APBCDC_CELL_TYPE; Purpose: Synchronizer cell option: 0 = bypass (simulation only), 1 = two D flip-flop cells, 2 = one 2-FF cell, 3 = one 3-FF cell, 4 = one 4-FF cell; Default: 2; Legal values / range: 0 to 4; Dependencies / invalid combinations: 0 is rejected by the SDC; Effect: Number of stages N = 2, 2, 3, 4 for the values 1 to 4
rules.statement: Value 0 (bypass) is for simulation only and is rejected by the SDC.

rules.quote: Parameter: LPARA_STRB_W; Purpose: Width of PSTRB; Default: Derived; Legal values / range: 1, 2 or 4; Dependencies / invalid combinations: PARA_APBCDC_DATA_W; Effect: DATA_W / 8
rules.statement: LPARA_STRB_W is derived as DATA_W / 8, giving 1, 2 or 4.

rules.quote: Parameter: LPARA_REQ_W; Purpose: Width of the request bundle; Default: Derived; Legal values / range: At least 7; Dependencies / invalid combinations: Parameters above; Effect: ADDR_W + 3 + 1 + STRB_W + DATA_W, plus USER_REQ_W and USER_DATA_W in APB5
rules.statement: LPARA_REQ_W equals ADDR_W + 3 + 1 + STRB_W + DATA_W, plus USER_REQ_W and USER_DATA_W in APB5, and is at least 7.

rules.quote: Parameter: LPARA_RESP_W; Purpose: Width of the response bundle; Default: Derived; Legal values / range: At least 9; Dependencies / invalid combinations: Parameters above; Effect: DATA_W + 1, plus USER_DATA_W and USER_RESP_W in APB5
rules.statement: LPARA_RESP_W equals DATA_W + 1, plus USER_DATA_W and USER_RESP_W in APB5, and is at least 9.

rules.quote: Illegal configurations are a data width other than 8, 16 or 32, an address width above 32 or equal to 0, a user width above its limit, a user width above 0 with PARA_APBCDC_APB5 = 0, and an option parameter outside its range. The IP does not check them and its behavior with them is not specified.
rules.statement: Illegal configurations (bad data/address width, user width over limit or with APB5 = 0, out-of-range options) must not be used; the IP does not check them and behavior is unspecified.

rules.quote: The bridge moves the fields unchanged and does no arithmetic.
rules.statement: The bridge must move the fields unchanged and perform no arithmetic on them.

rules.quote: Quantity: Address; Width: PARA_APBCDC_ADDR_W; Encoding / range: Byte address; Extension / truncation: None; Overflow / invalid behavior: Not applicable
rules.statement: The address is a byte address of width PARA_APBCDC_ADDR_W and is forwarded without extension or truncation.

rules.quote: Quantity: Data word; Width: PARA_APBCDC_DATA_W; Encoding / range: Opaque; Extension / truncation: None; Overflow / invalid behavior: Not applicable
rules.statement: The data word of width PARA_APBCDC_DATA_W is opaque and is forwarded without extension or truncation.

rules.quote: Quantity: Write strobes; Width: LPARA_STRB_W; Encoding / range: One bit per byte lane, bit n for PWDATA bits 8n+7 to 8n; Extension / truncation: None; Overflow / invalid behavior: Forwarded as received
rules.statement: Write strobes have width LPARA_STRB_W, one bit per byte lane (bit n for PWDATA bits 8n+7 to 8n), and are forwarded as received without extension or truncation.

rules.quote: Quantity: Protection; Width: 3; Encoding / range: As APB (bit 0 privileged, bit 1 non-secure, bit 2 instruction); Extension / truncation: None; Overflow / invalid behavior: Forwarded as received
rules.statement: Protection is 3 bits wide, encoded as APB (bit 0 privileged, bit 1 non-secure, bit 2 instruction), and forwarded as received.

rules.quote: Quantity: Request bundle; Width: LPARA_REQ_W; Encoding / range: Field order from the least significant bit: PADDR, PPROT, PWRITE, PSTRB, PWDATA, PAUSER, PWUSER; Extension / truncation: A field of width 0 contributes no bit; Overflow / invalid behavior: Not applicable
rules.statement: The request bundle of width LPARA_REQ_W packs fields from the least significant bit in order PADDR, PPROT, PWRITE, PSTRB, PWDATA, PAUSER, PWUSER; a zero-width field contributes no bit.

rules.quote: Quantity: Response bundle; Width: LPARA_RESP_W; Encoding / range: Field order from the least significant bit: PRDATA, PSLVERR, PRUSER, PBUSER; Extension / truncation: A field of width 0 contributes no bit; Overflow / invalid behavior: Not applicable
rules.statement: The response bundle of width LPARA_RESP_W packs fields from the least significant bit in order PRDATA, PSLVERR, PRUSER, PBUSER; a zero-width field contributes no bit.

rules.quote: Quantity: Request and acknowledge bits; Width: 1; Encoding / range: Two-phase: the value toggles per transfer, equal when idle. Four-phase: 1 while a phase is requested, 0 when idle; Extension / truncation: None; Overflow / invalid behavior: Not applicable
rules.statement: Request and acknowledge bits are 1 bit wide; in two-phase mode the value toggles per transfer and the request and acknowledge are equal when idle.

rules.quote: Quantity: Request and acknowledge bits; Width: 1; Encoding / range: Two-phase: the value toggles per transfer, equal when idle. Four-phase: 1 while a phase is requested, 0 when idle; Extension / truncation: None; Overflow / invalid behavior: Not applicable
rules.statement: In four-phase mode the request and acknowledge bit is 1 while a phase is requested and 0 when idle.

rules.quote: Mode/state: ENUM_ST_IDLE; Entry condition: Reset, or the end of RESP; Behavior: Waits for the Setup phase; Exit condition: i_apb_psel high and i_apb_penable low: WAIT; Outputs / side effects: At the exit edge: reg_req_payload loaded, reg_req toggled (two-phase) or set (four-phase)
rules.condition: mst FSM in ENUM_ST_IDLE with i_apb_psel high and i_apb_penable low
rules.statement: The requester FSM must leave IDLE to WAIT, loading reg_req_payload and toggling reg_req (two-phase) or setting it (four-phase) at the exit edge.

rules.quote: Mode/state: ENUM_ST_WAIT; Entry condition: Request launched; Behavior: Waits for the acknowledge event: two-phase, synchronized acknowledge equal to reg_req; four-phase, synchronized acknowledge high; Exit condition: Two-phase: event, load the response output registers, raise o_apb_pready: RESP. Four-phase: event, clear reg_req: CLOSE; Outputs / side effects: o_apb_pready 0
rules.statement: In WAIT the requester must keep o_apb_pready low; on the acknowledge event it goes to RESP (two-phase, raising o_apb_pready) or clears reg_req and goes to CLOSE (four-phase).

rules.quote: Mode/state: ENUM_ST_CLOSE; Entry condition: Four-phase, acknowledge seen; Behavior: Waits for the synchronized acknowledge to fall; Exit condition: Acknowledge low: load the response output registers, raise o_apb_pready: RESP; Outputs / side effects: reg_req 0
rules.statement: In CLOSE reg_req must be 0; when the synchronized acknowledge falls the FSM loads the response registers, raises o_apb_pready and goes to RESP.

rules.quote: Mode/state: ENUM_ST_RESP; Entry condition: Response loaded; Behavior: o_apb_pready is high for this cycle; Exit condition: Always: IDLE; Outputs / side effects: At the exit edge: o_apb_pready and o_apb_pslverr cleared
rules.statement: In RESP o_apb_pready must be high for one cycle, then the FSM returns to IDLE and clears o_apb_pready and o_apb_pslverr at the exit edge.

rules.quote: Mode/state: ENUM_ST_IDLE; Entry condition: Reset, or the end of a transfer; Behavior: Waits for the request event: two-phase, synchronized request different from reg_ack; four-phase, synchronized request high; Exit condition: Event: SETUP; Outputs / side effects: At the exit edge: reg_apb_payload loaded from the request bundle, o_apb_psel high
rules.condition: slv FSM in ENUM_ST_IDLE and request event seen (two-phase: synchronized request differs from reg_ack; four-phase: synchronized request high)
rules.statement: The completer FSM must go to SETUP, loading reg_apb_payload from the request bundle and driving o_apb_psel high at the exit edge.

rules.quote: Mode/state: ENUM_ST_SETUP; Entry condition: Request loaded; Behavior: Setup phase, o_apb_penable low; Exit condition: Always: ACCESS; Outputs / side effects: At the exit edge: o_apb_penable high
rules.statement: In SETUP o_apb_penable must be low; the FSM always moves to ACCESS and sets o_apb_penable high at the exit edge.

rules.quote: Mode/state: ENUM_ST_ACCESS; Entry condition: Setup phase done; Behavior: Access phase; waits for i_apb_pready; Exit condition: i_apb_pready high: two-phase IDLE, four-phase REQ0; Outputs / side effects: At the exit edge: reg_resp_hold loaded, o_apb_psel and o_apb_penable low, reg_ack toggled (two-phase) or set (four-phase)
rules.condition: slv FSM in ENUM_ST_ACCESS and i_apb_pready high
rules.statement: On i_apb_pready high the FSM must load reg_resp_hold, drop o_apb_psel and o_apb_penable, toggle (two-phase) or set (four-phase) reg_ack, and go to IDLE (two-phase) or REQ0 (four-phase).

rules.quote: Mode/state: ENUM_ST_REQ0; Entry condition: Four-phase, acknowledge launched; Behavior: Waits for the synchronized request to fall; Exit condition: Request low: IDLE; Outputs / side effects: At the exit edge: reg_ack cleared
rules.condition: slv FSM in ENUM_ST_REQ0 and synchronized request low (four-phase)
rules.statement: In REQ0 the FSM must wait for the synchronized request to fall, then clear reg_ack and go to IDLE.

rules.quote: Operation ID: OP-001; Inputs / preconditions: Setup phase with PWRITE = 1 on the requester side, mst FSM in IDLE; Processing semantics: Capture the fields, cross the request, run one APB write on the completer side, return the response; Result / completion: Completer written, PREADY for one cycle; Latency / ordering: Bound of REQ-PERF-001 or REQ-PERF-002
rules.condition: Setup phase with PWRITE=1, mst FSM in IDLE
rules.statement: The bridge must capture the fields, cross the request, run one APB write on the completer side and return the response, with PREADY for one cycle.

rules.quote: Operation ID: OP-002; Inputs / preconditions: Setup phase with PWRITE = 0; Processing semantics: As OP-001 for a read; PRDATA and PRUSER are returned; Result / completion: Read data returned with PREADY; Latency / ordering: Same bound
rules.statement: For a read the bridge must return PRDATA and PRUSER to the requester with PREADY.

rules.quote: Operation ID: OP-003; Inputs / preconditions: Completer holds PREADY low for w cycles; Processing semantics: The completer-side Access phase lasts w + 1 cycles; Result / completion: Requester-side PREADY after the response; Latency / ordering: Bound grows by w completer cycles
rules.condition: completer holds PREADY low for w cycles
rules.statement: The completer-side Access phase must last w + 1 cycles and requester-side PREADY must follow after the response.

rules.quote: Operation ID: OP-004; Inputs / preconditions: Completer drives PSLVERR with PREADY; Processing semantics: PSLVERR is part of the response bundle; Result / completion: PSLVERR high in the PREADY cycle of the requester; Latency / ordering: Same bound
rules.statement: PSLVERR must be carried in the response bundle and be high in the requester-side PREADY cycle.

rules.quote: Operation ID: OP-005; Inputs / preconditions: Next Setup phase in the cycle after PREADY; Processing semantics: The mst FSM is back in IDLE and captures it; Result / completion: Second transfer starts at once; Latency / ordering: One transfer at a time
rules.condition: next Setup phase in the cycle after PREADY
rules.statement: The mst FSM must be back in IDLE and capture the Setup phase immediately, starting the second transfer at once; one transfer at a time.

rules.quote: Operation ID: OP-006; Inputs / preconditions: APB5, i_apb_pwakeup or a transfer in progress; Processing semantics: o_apb_pwakeup follows the synchronized wake-up OR the in-progress term; Result / completion: o_apb_pwakeup high before or with o_apb_psel; Latency / ordering: Synchronizer latency of N cycles of CLK-SLV
rules.condition: APB5, i_apb_pwakeup or a transfer in progress
rules.statement: o_apb_pwakeup must follow the synchronized wake-up OR the in-progress term and be high before or with o_apb_psel.

rules.quote: Operation ID: OP-007; Inputs / preconditions: APB5 with user widths above 0; Processing semantics: PAUSER and PWUSER travel in the request bundle, PRUSER and PBUSER in the response bundle; Result / completion: Same values on the other side; Latency / ordering: As OP-001
rules.statement: PAUSER and PWUSER must cross in the request bundle and PRUSER and PBUSER in the response bundle, with identical values on the other side.

rules.quote: Operation ID: OP-008; Inputs / preconditions: i_rst_n_mst or i_rst_n_slv low; Processing semantics: Asynchronous clear of the state of the domain; Result / completion: All registers at the reset value, transfer in flight lost; Latency / ordering: Immediate
rules.statement: State of the domain must clear asynchronously, all registers at reset value, and a transfer in flight is lost.

rules.quote: Operation ID: OP-009; Inputs / preconditions: PARA_APBCDC_HS_TYPE = 1; Processing semantics: The four-phase handshake of OP-001 and OP-002; Result / completion: Same result as OP-001 and OP-002, slower; Latency / ordering: Bound of REQ-PERF-002
rules.statement: The bridge must use the four-phase handshake and give the same results as OP-001 and OP-002.

rules.quote: Cycle / event: Setup edge E0 (end of the Setup cycle); Input condition: i_apb_psel high, i_apb_penable low, mst FSM in IDLE; State/action: Request bundle loaded, request bit launched, FSM to WAIT; Output condition: o_apb_pready stays low
rules.condition: Setup edge E0 with mst FSM in IDLE
rules.statement: At E0 the request bundle must be loaded, the request bit launched, FSM to WAIT, and o_apb_pready stay low.

rules.quote: Cycle / event: First N + 1 edges of i_clk_slv after E0; Input condition: Request bit in the synchronizer; State/action: The slv FSM sees the event at edge N + 1 and loads reg_apb_payload; Output condition: o_apb_psel high after that edge Cycle / event: Next two edges of i_clk_slv; Input condition: None; State/action: SETUP, then ACCESS; Output condition: o_apb_penable high from the second
rules.statement: The slv FSM must see the event at edge N+1 of i_clk_slv, load reg_apb_payload, raise o_apb_psel, then pass SETUP and ACCESS, with o_apb_penable high from the second edge.

rules.quote: Cycle / event: Edge of i_apb_pready; Input condition: i_apb_pready high in ACCESS; State/action: Response held, acknowledge launched; Output condition: o_apb_psel, o_apb_penable low
rules.statement: At the i_apb_pready edge the response must be held, acknowledge launched, and o_apb_psel and o_apb_penable low.

rules.quote: Cycle / event: N + 1 edges of i_clk_mst after the acknowledge launch; Input condition: Acknowledge in the synchronizer; State/action: The mst FSM sees the event, loads the response, raises o_apb_pready; Output condition: o_apb_pready high for one cycle, then FSM to IDLE
rules.condition: N+1 i_clk_mst edges after acknowledge launch
rules.statement: The mst FSM must load the response and raise o_apb_pready for one cycle, then go to IDLE.

rules.quote: There is no arbitration: one requester-side interface and one completer-side interface, one transfer at a time (DEC-013).
rules.statement: The bridge has no arbitration: one requester-side interface and one completer-side interface, handling one transfer at a time.

rules.quote: A new Setup phase that the requester drives before PREADY cannot occur (APB is non-pipelined).
rules.condition: A transfer is in progress and PREADY has not yet completed it
rules.statement: A new Setup phase must not be driven by the requester before PREADY, since APB is non-pipelined.

rules.quote: Handshake: Two-phase; Upper bound of D: (N + 3) x T_mst + (N + 3 + w) x T_slv; Equal clocks, N stages, w wait states: 2N + 6 + w cycles
rules.condition: Two-phase handshake, N synchronizer stages, w completer wait states
rules.statement: Duration D from first Setup cycle to end of PREADY cycle must not exceed (N+3)xT_mst + (N+3+w)xT_slv; for equal clocks 2N+6+w cycles.

rules.quote: Handshake: Four-phase; Upper bound of D: (2N + 4) x T_mst + (2N + 4 + w) x T_slv; Equal clocks, N stages, w wait states: 4N + 8 + w cycles
rules.condition: Four-phase handshake, N synchronizer stages, w completer wait states
rules.statement: Duration D from first Setup cycle to end of PREADY cycle must not exceed (2N+4)xT_mst + (2N+4+w)xT_slv; for equal clocks 4N+8+w cycles.

rules.quote: One transfer per D; no pipelining.
rules.statement: Throughput is one transfer per duration D, with no pipelining of transfers.

rules.quote: Not required (confirmed by user, 2026-10-25): the IP contains no memory or macro; the only storage is the registers of the two bundles and the control flip-flops (Section 5.1).
rules.statement: The IP must contain no memory or macro; the only storage is the registers of the two bundles and the control flip-flops.

rules.quote: Not required (confirmed by user, 2026-10-25): the IP has no software-visible registers; it is configured by parameters (Section 8).
rules.statement: The IP must not provide software-visible registers; it is configured only by parameters (Section 8).

rules.statement: The bridge must forward the completer PSLVERR so that o_apb_pslverr is high in the o_apb_pready cycle.

rules.quote: Error ID: ERR-001; Detection condition: Completer drives PSLVERR with PREADY; Observable response/status: Forwarded: o_apb_pslverr high in the o_apb_pready cycle; Interrupt: None; Clear/recovery: The next transfer is independent; Reset behavior: Not applicable
rules.condition: After a transfer completed with PSLVERR
rules.statement: The next transfer must be independent of a previous transfer that completed with an error.

rules.quote: Error ID: ERR-002; Detection condition: Completer never drives PREADY; Observable response/status: The bridge waits without limit; the requester sees PREADY low; Interrupt: None; Clear/recovery: A system watchdog or a reset of both domains (DEC-006); Reset behavior: Cleared by reset
rules.statement: The bridge must wait without limit for PREADY, and the requester sees PREADY low during the wait.

rules.quote: Error ID: ERR-002; Detection condition: Completer never drives PREADY; Observable response/status: The bridge waits without limit; the requester sees PREADY low; Interrupt: None; Clear/recovery: A system watchdog or a reset of both domains (DEC-006); Reset behavior: Cleared by reset
rules.statement: The hang condition is cleared by reset; recovery is by a system watchdog or a reset of both domains.

rules.quote: Error ID: ERR-003; Detection condition: Reset asserted while a transfer is in flight; Observable response/status: The transfer is lost; the requester model repeats it after the release; Interrupt: None; Clear/recovery: Release both resets, restart the transfer; Reset behavior: Clears all state
rules.condition: Reset asserted while a transfer is in flight
rules.statement: The in-flight transfer must be lost and all state cleared; both resets must be released and the transfer restarted.

rules.quote: Error ID: ERR-004; Detection condition: Requester breaks the APB rules (Setup without Access, change of a field during Access, PENABLE without Setup); Observable response/status: Not detected; the bridge uses the values of the Setup cycle, and ignores PENABLE without a Setup (DEC-027); Interrupt: None; Clear/recovery: The integrator fixes the requester; Reset behavior: Not applicable
rules.condition: Requester breaks APB rules by Setup without Access, field change during Access, or PENABLE without Setup
rules.statement: The bridge must use the values of the Setup cycle and must ignore PENABLE without a Setup; the violation is not detected.

rules.quote: Error ID: ERR-005; Detection condition: One reset asserted alone, or illegal parameter value; Observable response/status: Not detected; behavior not specified; Interrupt: None; Clear/recovery: The integrator fixes the integration; Reset behavior: Not applicable
rules.condition: One reset asserted alone, or illegal parameter value
rules.statement: Behavior is not specified and no detection is provided; integrators must not rely on any behavior when only one reset is asserted or a parameter is illegal.

rules.quote: There is no sticky error, no error counter and no error output other than PSLVERR.
rules.statement: The bridge must have no sticky error, no error counter and no error output other than PSLVERR.

rules.quote: There is no data protection (no parity or ECC), so a corrupted bundle bit is not detected.
rules.statement: The bridge has no data protection (parity or ECC), so a corrupted bundle bit is not detected.

rules.statement: Four-phase transfer duration must be at most (2N + 4) x T_mst + (2N + 4 + w) x T_slv.

The IP carries one AMBA APB transfer at a time from an APB requester in clock domain MST to an APB completer in clock domain SLV.
The two clocks are asynchronous to each other: any frequency ratio and any phase (DEC-008).

The bridge is an APB completer on its requester-side interface and an APB requester on its completer-side interface; the two interfaces are named by the clock domain suffix mst and slv (DEC-001, rule PRT-02).
APB allows only one transfer in flight, so the bridge is not a FIFO: a handshake with bundled data crosses the domains (DEC-002).

The requester-side logic captures the request fields once, in the Setup phase, into a hold register and launches a request bit; the completer-side logic sees the request after a synchronizer, loads the fields into its own register, runs one normal APB transfer, holds the response, and returns an acknowledge bit; the requester-side logic sees the acknowledge after a synchronizer and returns the response.
Only the one-bit request, acknowledge and wake-up signals pass through synchronizers.
The handshake is selectable: a two-phase (toggle) handshake or a four-phase (level) handshake (parameter PARA_APBCDC_HS_TYPE, DEC-005).
The interface is APB4 or APB5 (parameter PARA_APBCDC_APB5, DEC-003).
Included:
APB4 transfers: PSEL, PENABLE, PWRITE, PADDR, PPROT, PSTRB, PWDATA, PREADY, PRDATA, PSLVERR, with wait states and error responses.
APB5 option: PWAKEUP, and the user signals PAUSER, PWUSER, PRUSER, PBUSER with configurable widths (width 0 = signal not present).
Two-phase and four-phase handshake, selectable at elaboration.
Synchronizer depth selectable at elaboration with the cell option of 001_AsyncGrayFIFO (PARA_APBCDC_CELL_TYPE).
Complete SDC for the crossing paths and the interfaces (Synopsys dialect, DEC-007).
Excluded:
Parity protection and the check signals of APB5 (DEC-003).
Several completers: one PSEL on the completer side, no address decode (DEC-013).
Timeout on the completer side: the bridge waits for PREADY without limit (DEC-006).

This subsection answers the question of the designer of 2026-10-25 and corrects an earlier statement of the author: -datapath_only is the Vivado (XDC) option and -ignore_clock_latency is the Synopsys option of the same purpose; the SDC of this IP uses the Synopsys form (DEC-007).
Why a bound and not a false path.
A false path or an asynchronous clock group removes every check from the bundle path, so place and route may route it arbitrarily long and the ordering is broken without a warning.
A bound on the data-path delay keeps the ordering true by construction (UG903, Constraining Asynchronous Signals, makes the same case for buses that are not Gray coded).
Why the default check is meaningless.

For two unrelated clocks the setup relationship is derived from the nearest launch and capture edges, which depend on a phase that is not fixed; the result is an arbitrary budget. set_max_delay replaces it by an absolute delay, independent of the edges.
Why the clock latency is ignored.
By default the tool counts the clock network latency and uncertainty in the budget.
Why (N - 1) x T_dst.

The destination FSM sees the control event after the control bit has passed N stages, that is at the destination edge number N after the first edge that samples it, and loads the bundle at the next edge.

In the worst case the first edge samples the bit right after launch, so the bundle has at least N destination periods; the budget (N - 1) x T_dst leaves one destination period as a guard band for what the option removed (clock latency difference, uncertainty) and for the setup time.
Why no hold check.
A hold check between unrelated clocks compares edges with no fixed relation.
The functional hold is guaranteed by the protocol: the bundle does not change until the handshake has completed. set_false_path -hold removes the meaningless check; the setup bound stays.
Why no bus-skew constraint. set_bus_skew is for buses that the destination samples at an unknown time (for example Gray pointers).
The bundles here are loaded only after the control event, so all bits only need to arrive before the load, which the maximum delay guarantees.
The control bits are single bits.
Why no clock group.

UG903 states that a clock group or a false path on the same paths makes the maximum-delay constraints ineffective; the SDC of this IP therefore leaves the clocks unrelated and covers every crossing by an exception, so that any other path between the domains is reported with the default relation and is found as a design error.
Synchronizer depth.

The SDC takes the depth N as a variable and refuses N below 2: the value PARA_APBCDC_CELL_TYPE = 0 has no stage, the bundle would have at most one destination period and the budget formula would give 0 or less.
